Among the four locations, ④ is located in the lower right of the figure, the sunrise time is later than 6 o’clock, and the sunshine duration is less than 12 hours; ② has a sunshine duration greater than 12 hours and an earlier sunrise; ③ is roughly near 6 o’clock, with sunshine of about close to or slightly less than 12 hours; ① also has sunrise earlier than near 6 o’clock. Reasoning: Around June 22, the direct rays of the sun are in the Northern Hemisphere; the Northern Hemisphere has longer days and shorter nights, manifested as sunshine duration greater than 12 hours and sunrise earlier than 6 o’clock; the Southern Hemisphere has shorter days and longer nights, manifested as sunshine duration less than 12 hours and sunrise later than 6 o’clock. The point in the figure that simultaneously conforms to “sunrise later than 6 o’clock” and “sunshine less than 12 hours” is ④. Therefore, the one located in the Southern Hemisphere is ④.
